provenance.notes: KIT: the kit's Component List photo reads 'ADS7830 Module x1' and the Potentiometer, Photoresistor and Adjustable Fan projects use it, so kitTags is 'kit'. SIM MODEL: sim.model is 'ads7830', its own model: the chip is 8-bit, with 8 single-ended or 4 differential channels, a command byte with SD, C2-C0 and PD1-PD0 bits instead of the ADS1115's config register, no PGA, and a 2.5 V internal reference that is off after power-up. PIN ORDER: the kit's module drawing (ADS7830_Module.png, a to-scale PCB render with the kit's table) shows a left column of eight pins A0 to A7 (top to bottom) and a right column VCC, SDA, SCL, GND (top to bottom); the kit's Fritzing wiring (2.1.4.png) shows the same four on one edge in the order GND, SCL, SDA, VCC. The pin order here follows the printed top-to-bottom order. The relative positions (right column 5 pitches from the left one and starting 2 pitches below A0) are measured from the PCB render using the 8-pin A0-A7 span as the scale (+-0.3 pitch). CONNECTOR: the kit's photo shows the module with pin headers attached, so the pins are modelled as male pins; the Potentiometer wiring diagram plugs the module straight into the breadboard. SUPPLY: the kit's table says 'VCC Power Supply, 3.3V or 5V'; the TI datasheet (SBAS302C) says 2.7 V to 5 V operation, with specified performance at 2.7-3.6 V and 4.75-5.25 V, absolute maximum 6 V on +VDD, and the digital input range -0.3 V to +VDD + 0.3 V. The kit's lesson describes the 3.3 V input range divided into 256 steps. I2C ADDRESS: the kit's table gives 0x48 for SCL and SDA ('IIC Serial Clock Address 0x48') and the lesson code probes 0x48. The TI datasheet sets the address by pins A1 and A0 (10010 A1 A0, so 0x48-0x4B), but this module breaks out no A0/A1 pins, so the address is fixed at 0x48 (the kit does not say how the pins are strapped). CONFLICT (different boards, seen only in search extracts, not opened directly): Freenove's ADS7830 module docs report 0x4B, and the Adafruit ADS7830 board has 10K pull-ups and address jumpers; neither is this LAFVIN module and neither is used. REFERENCE: the TI datasheet gives a built-in 2.5 V reference/buffer, off by default at power-up, and a full-scale input span of 0 to VREF; the module's REFIN wiring is not documented in the kit pages, so the effective full-scale voltage is unverified (the kit's lesson says 3.3 V). 8 CHANNELS: A0-A7 are CH0-CH7 (the kit table 'Analog input channels 1-8'); the chip's COM pin and the single-ended/differential choice are not broken out. ON-BOARD PARTS: the PCB render shows LED1 (power indicator), resistors R1, R2, R3 and capacitor C1 beside the TSSOP-16 chip. NOT VERIFIED: the kit publishes no schematic, so whether R2/R3 are I2C pull-ups, to which rail, and their value are unknown (i2cPullupVerified is false); the module may pull SDA and SCL up to VCC, which would put 5 V on the I2C lines if the module is powered from 5 V (SPEC 8 OVERVOLTAGE_GPIO) - run it from the Pi's 3.3 V as the kit does. SIZE: no mechanical drawing exists in the opened sources; the board size is measured from the PCB render with the 2.54 mm pin pitch as the scale (+-1 mm) and the height is only the TSSOP-16 package maximum of 1.2 mm from the TI package drawing (PCB thickness not included).
